Elements of a Set
Every element of a set belongs to that set.
The symbol "e" is used to show that an element "belongs to" the set. For example, for the
set A= (10, 15, 20, 35). we can say that 10 e A.

The elements of a set must be distinct. Distinct elements mean the elements which are
unique in themselves when compared to the other objects of the set. In simple words,
we can say that the objects are said to be distinct if they do not appear more than once in a
set.
Example 3:
Let's consider a set of alphabets in the word "student" denoted by the letter R.
R= (s, t, u, d, e, n, t)
Here letter "t" appeared twice but we will write it one time as below.
R= (s, t, u, d, e, n)
If we write it twice then the elements of this set will not be distinct.
Cardinality of a Set
The cardinality of a set shows the number of the elements of the set.
For example, for the set B = (3, 6, 9, 12), the cardinality of set B is 4 as it has 4 elements.
Symbolically we can write it as: n(B) = 4. We read it as the number of elements of set B is 4.
